scientific_question: Does the frozen WebShop action contract remain unusable because Qwen2.5-3B lacks the base-agent capability needed for product selection, or is the failure shared by comparable small instruction models?
hypothesis: A larger or capability-diverse base model will show a selective fresh-task closed-loop advantage under the same WebShop contract; if every model remains at zero, the evidence favors a benchmark/interface or task-content bottleneck rather than Qwen2.5-3B scale alone.
frozen_variables: action parser and fallback validity rule
no training, teacher, memory, retrieval, adapter, or outcome-based tuning
same single-GPU runtime and explicit UUID binding
primary_metrics: valid qualified-positive rate by model and task
mean final task score over valid attempts

provenance.model_assets: manifest-bound local model paths and inventory digests in H1.27_TASK_MANIFEST.json
provenance.upstream_audit: stable unchanged; PR #297 SD-LoRA-RR and PR #298 MemEvolve remain draft and are not used

stop_rule: Stop after all 64 valid formal attempts or after the 4 GPU-hour cap; operational failures are preserved and excluded, then repaired only before a fresh formal start.
positive_branch: If one model selectively exceeds QWEN25-3B across at least two task identities and paired seeds, preregister an independent confirmation on new tasks before interpreting Q3; do not claim OpenEvo efficacy.
negative_branch: If all models remain at zero or gains are task-local, close the scale-only question and design an explicitly scoped experience-content or task-family study; do not sweep prompt, carrier, rank, LR, or epoch.
claim_boundary: Base-agent capability diagnostic only. It cannot open Q3, H2, D0, retention/transfer, or SEED.

tracking.offline_fallback: only after exact online initialization/upload failure with preserved error and spool hash

required_runtime_contract: no compute apps on selected UUID
